name: Safety Beach
intro: Safety Beach is the long shallow crescent between Mount Martha and Dromana  -  the kind of bay beach where the water is calm enough for very small children and the ridge behind it is steep enough to put you among vineyards in under ten minutes. For most of its history it was a quiet caravan-and-holiday-house stretch; in the last decade it has slowly sharpened, with a marina at the western end, a handful of smarter houses lining the foreshore, and a couple of genuinely good food stops using the view properly. It is a useful place to stay for anyone who wants a base that works equally for beach mornings and hinterland afternoons.
factualLede: Safety Beach is a bayside township on the Mornington Peninsula's eastern Port Phillip shoreline, 70 km from Melbourne, between Dromana and Mount Martha, with a marina and a sheltered swimming beach.

heroImage.alt: Safety Beach foreshore with Arthurs Seat rising behind

tldr: Safety Beach is a long, calm bay foreshore between Mount Martha and Dromana — shallow water makes it the Peninsula's best swimming spot for young children.
Best for: families with toddlers; anyone who wants calm water and easy beach access without driving to the crowded spots.
Signature experience: morning on the foreshore, then ten minutes up the hill to a cellar door or the Arthurs Seat gondola.
Half a day; usually paired with Dromana.
notFor: anyone wanting a distinct town centre
worstTime: windless holiday afternoons when the foreshore is packed
stayDuration: half a day to one night
signature: The calmest broad bay foreshore on the Peninsula, with the ridge rising straight behind it.
skip: Expecting a village atmosphere — Safety Beach works as a foreshore, not a town.
bestDay: Early beach with kids, coffee near the marina, long lunch in Dromana or up on the ridge, back for sunset.
insiderNote: The water stays shallower for longer here than almost anywhere else on the bay side, which is exactly why local families keep coming back.
